vulnerabilities.description: GNU Wget does not validate the IP address provided by an FTP PASV response while operating in FTP passive mode. A malicious FTP server, or an HTTP server that redirects to an FTP URL, can exploit this behavior to redirect Wget's data connection to an arbitrary IP address and port. This allows an attacker to forge server-side requests from the machine running Wget, potentially accessing localhost services or internal network resources.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure uses wget only for fixed HTTPS downloads during image build and not in its runtime path.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable behavior requires Wget FTP passive-mode transfers, while Liquibase Secure uses wget only for fixed HTTPS downloads at image build time and not at runtime.

analysis.detail: The scanned image reports wget 1.21.4-1ubuntu4.1, below Ubuntu's fixed 1.21.4-1ubuntu4.4, but this issue requires Wget to follow an attacker-controlled FTP passive-mode data connection. Liquibase Secure uses wget only during image build to fetch its release tarball and the lpm zip over HTTPS, and it does not invoke wget at container runtime.

vulnerabilities.description: GNU Wget through 1.21.1 does not omit the Authorization header upon a redirect to a different origin, a related issue to CVE-2018-1000007.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. wget is not invoked at container runtime.

ratings.justification: wget only runs at Docker build time against hardcoded, sha256-verified URLs; never invoked at runtime.

analysis.detail: wget path-traversal-via-redirect issue (Authorization header leaked cross-origin on redirect). wget is only invoked at Docker build time against hardcoded repo.liquibase.com/GitHub URLs that are sha256-verified after download (docker/Dockerfile:27, docker/Dockerfile:55). No runtime code in docker-entrypoint.sh or the Liquibase CLI invokes wget.

vulnerabilities.description: GNU wget is vulnerable to denial of service in its FTP OPIE/S-KEY authentication functionality. The server-supplied sequence number from the FTP challenge line is used as an iteration count for an MD5 key- derivation loop without any upper bound validation. A malicious FTP server or a network attacker positioned to intercept FTP traffic can send a crafted OPIE challenge with a sequence number near INT_MAX, causing wget to perform up to approximately 2.1 billion MD5 computations and suspend for some time. The --timeout option does not mitigate this because it applies only to network I/O, not CPU computation. This issue was fixed in commit e9697d98e7249b0f68a6be040a4f3dcc5bc101fa
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. wget is not invoked at container runtime.

ratings.justification: wget only runs at Docker build time against hardcoded, sha256-verified HTTPS URLs; never invoked at runtime, and no FTP transfers occur in this image.

analysis.detail: wget FTP OPIE/S-KEY authentication denial-of-service issue, with an upstream patch not yet backported to Ubuntu noble. wget is only invoked at Docker build time against hardcoded, sha256-verified URLs (docker/Dockerfile:27, docker/Dockerfile:55); never invoked at runtime, and this image never performs FTP transfers.

vulnerabilities.description: Applications that use Wget to access a remote resource using shorthand URLs and pass arbitrary user credentials in the URL are vulnerable. In these cases attackers can enter crafted credentials which will cause Wget to access an arbitrary host.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. wget is not invoked at container runtime.

ratings.justification: wget only runs at Docker build time against hardcoded, credential- free, sha256-verified URLs; never invoked at runtime.

analysis.detail: wget shorthand-URL credential-confusion issue (fixed only in Ubuntu 26.04/resolute, not noble). wget is only invoked at Docker build time against hardcoded, sha256-verified URLs with no embedded credentials (docker/Dockerfile:27, docker/Dockerfile:55); never invoked at runtime.

vulnerabilities.description: GNU Wget through 1.25.0, fixed in commit 37a40fc, contains a heap buffer underread vulnerability in the clean_metalink_string() function within src/metalink.c that allows a malicious server to trigger memory corruption by serving a Metalink document containing a whitespace-only URL. Attackers can cause the function to decrement a pointer past the start of the buffer when processing an all-whitespace Metalink URL, potentially leading to abnormal program behavior.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not invoke wget at runtime.

ratings.justification: wget is used only while the image is built and is never invoked at runtime, so the vulnerable parser is never reached.

analysis.detail: wget is present in the image because the Dockerfile uses it to download the Liquibase Secure release tarball and lpm while the image is built. Nothing runs it afterwards: the container entrypoint and the liquibase launcher script contain no wget invocation, the Liquibase CLI is a Java process that uses the JDK HTTP client for its own downloads, and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. The vulnerable Metalink parser only runs inside a wget process fetching attacker-controlled Metalink content, so it is not reachable from Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu wget 1.21.2-2ubuntu1.3 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and 1.21.4-1ubuntu4.3 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.1); Liquibase Secure 5.2.2 ships 1.21.4-1ubuntu4.5.

vulnerabilities.description: GNU Wget through 1.25.0, fixed in commit 43d3ba9, contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the parse_content_range() function within src/http.c that allows server-controlled values to cause signed integer arithmetic to overflow. Attackers can supply malicious Content-Range header values to trigger undefined behavior and download desynchronization in the affected client.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not invoke wget at runtime.

ratings.justification: wget is used only while the image is built and is never invoked at runtime, so the vulnerable parser is never reached.

vulnerabilities.description: GNU Wget through 1.25.0, fixed in commit c2640fe, contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the convert_fname() function within src/url.c that allows remote attackers to trigger memory corruption through a server-supplied filename requiring character set conversion. When the output buffer is too small during iconv E2BIG reallocation, the reallocation logic miscalculates the remaining space, leading to a heap buffer overflow that can be exploited via a maliciously crafted server response.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not invoke wget at runtime.

vulnerabilities.description: GNU Wget through 1.25.0, fixed in commit dd692d9, contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the html_quote_string() function in src/convert.c that allows a remote attacker to trigger memory corruption by supplying a crafted HTML attribute with a large number of characters requiring entity encoding. A server-supplied HTML attribute causes a signed integer counter to overflow during output size accumulation, resulting in an undersized heap allocation and subsequent heap buffer overflow during the copy phase.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not invoke wget at runtime.
